edits.english: The Gemara elaborates on a matter raised earlier. And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, who hold one tribe that performs a transgression liable because it is considered a congregation, from where do they derive that one tribe is characterized as a congregation? The Sages say that it is derived from a verse, as it is written: “And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem before the new courtyard in the house of the Lord” (II Chronicles 20:5). The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of “new” in this verse? Rabbi Yoḥanan says that on that occasion they introduced new matters and said: One who was ritually impure who immersed that day and is waiting for nightfall for the purification process to be completed may not enter even the Levite camp. From the fact that the verse employs the term “congregation” in reference to Judah and Jerusalem, it can be inferred that one tribe is characterized as a congregation.
Since it is written 'congregation of Judah,' it implies that one tribe is called a congregation.

Thus, the tribe of Judah alone is called a congregation (Rashi). It must be said that Rabbi Meir would argue against this proof, saying that one tribe is called 'congregation of Judah' but is not called simply 'congregation' (Chak Natan and others).

According to Torah law, a tovul yom is permitted to enter the Levite camp (which includes the Women's Courtyard in the Temple). He is only forbidden from entering the 'Camp of the Divine Presence' — the holy area in the Temple, the Ulam, the Heichal, etc. (Meiri). The Be'er Sheva cited in the name of Tosafot Pesachim that they did not decree concerning the entire Levite camp, because they did not decree a prohibition for a tovul yom to enter the Temple Mount (which is also part of the Levite camp), but only the Courtyard.

A tovul yom is sent away from the Women's Courtyard, but not one who lacks atonement. The prohibition for a tovul yom to enter the Levite camp is by rabbinic decree, in accordance with the words of Rabbi Yochanan (Rambam, Sefer Avoda, Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 3:6).

Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov objects to this: From where do you draw this conclusion? Perhaps Jerusalem is different, as Jerusalem was also in the tribal land of Benjamin. Accordingly, it was shared by two tribes. Rather, Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said that proof that a tribe is characterized as a congregation is derived from another verse, as it is written that Jacob recounted what God said to him when he returned from Paddan: “And said to me: Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a congregation of peoples” (Genesis 48:4). Who was born to Jacob from that time on? Only Benjamin. Conclude from it that this is what the Merciful One is saying to Jacob: Another congregation shall be now born to you. Apparently, one tribe is characterized as a congregation.

edits.hebrew: ודלמא שאני שבט יהודה דהוה עמיה בירושלים שבט בנימין: - ושני שבטים הוא דאקרי קהל אבל שבט אחד לא:

edits.english: Perhaps the tribe of Judah is different, as the tribe of Benjamin was with it in Jerusalem. And two tribes are called a congregation, but not one tribe.

edits.hebrew: אלא מהכא הנני מפרך והרביתיך ונתתיך לקהל עמים וגו': - והיכא אמר ליה הכי דכתיב וירא אלהים אל יעקב עוד בבואו מפדן ארם וגו' וכתיב ויאמר לו אלהים אני אל שדי פרה ורבה גוי וקהל גוים יהיה ממך וגו':

edits.english: Rather, from here: 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a congregation of peoples,' etc. And where did He say this to Jacob? As it is written: 'And God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram,' etc., and it is written: 'And God said to him: "I am God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall come from you," ' etc.

edits.hebrew: מאן הוה אתיליד ליה בההיא שעתא: - כלומר מאן הוה עתיד למילד ההיא שעתא בנימין ושמע מינה דקאמר ליה רחמנא השתא מתיליד לך קהל אחרינא:

edits.english: Who was born to Jacob at that time? Meaning, who was destined to be born to Jacob at that time? Benjamin. And learn from it that the Merciful One said to Jacob: 'Another congregation shall be born to you now.'

For Jerusalem was originally mostly in the inheritance of the tribe of Benjamin, and the members of the tribe of Benjamin were with the tribe of Judah during the First Temple period. Thus, there were two tribes there, and we do not learn from here that only one tribe is called a congregation (Rashi). The commentators have already discussed the explanation of the Rambam's words, who brings this verse as proof for the view that one tribe is called a congregation. And some have written that since the verse explicitly mentions only the tribe of Judah, it implies that one tribe is called a congregation (Rabbi Moshe Adawi).

And Tosafot wondered: Why does the Gemara bring this verse, which is later, when it was possible to bring a clearer verse, which is also earlier, and is directly from the words of God: 'Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall come from you' (Genesis 35:11). See in the commentators who tried to resolve this difficulty in various ways. Indeed, Rabbeinu Chananel in his commentary does bring the earlier verse. And similarly, in the Jerusalem Talmud, this verse is simply brought as a proof.

edits.hebrew: הנני מפרך והרביתיך וגו': - תימה דשביק קרא דאמר הקב"ה ליעקב גוי וקהל גוים יהיה ממך:

edits.english: 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you,' etc. It is astounding that the Gemara abandons the verse where the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Jacob: 'A nation and a company of nations shall come from you.'

Rav Shabba said to Rav Kahana: Perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying to Jacob: It is when Benjamin is born to Jacob that Jacob will have twelve tribes, who are together characterized as a congregation. Rav Kahana said to Rav Shabba: But is that to say that twelve tribes are characterized as a congregation, and eleven tribes are not characterized as a congregation? It has already been established that even two tribes are characterized as a congregation. Rather, it is apparent from this verse that even one tribe is characterized as a congregation.

edits.hebrew: י"א שבטים לא: - בתמיהה והא אמרת דשני שבטים איקרו קהל יהודה ובנימין אלא ודאי הכי קאמר ליה דהשתא מתיליד לך קהל אחרינא אלמא שבט בנימין לבדו איקרי קהל:

edits.english: Eleven tribes are not? In wonderment: But you said that two tribes are called a congregation, Judah and Benjamin! Rather, it certainly means that the Merciful One said to Jacob: 'Another congregation shall be born to you now,' implying that the tribe of Benjamin alone is called a congregation.

Rashi explains that it is impossible to say so, because from the verse 'congregation of Judah and Jerusalem' we learn that even two tribes are called a congregation (and see in Maharsha what he questioned about it). And some simply said that it is certain that most of the tribes of Israel are called a congregation (see Rabbeinu Chananel).
